summary.headline: FY26 was Lemon Tree's best year: revenue Rs 1,452.7 crore (+13%), PAT Rs 288.3 crore (+19%), with margin down 126 bps to 48.1%.
summary.overview: Lemon Tree reported record FY26 and Q4 FY26 on occupancy, ARR, revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT and cash profit, with Q4 revenue of Rs 419.5 crore (+11%) and PAT of Rs 116.5 crore (+8%). Net EBITDA margin fell to 48.1% for FY26 and 52% for Q4, which management attributes to renovation spend, technology investment and the GST change. Management guided that these three cost heads fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28, and set out a proposed demerger that would leave Lemon Tree as an asset-light entity and Fleur Hotels as an owner/lessor platform. Q4 demand softened in March and April from the Middle East conflict and airline disruption, with corporate travel weaker and occupancy hitting what management called a ceiling.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever for a full financial year
from Rs 1,699 crore a year ago

segments.name: Lemon Tree (asset-light, managed and franchised)
segments.commentary: Opened 20 managed/franchised hotels (1,523 rooms) and signed 55 (4,912 rooms) in FY26; total pipeline 22,581 rooms across 268 hotels, of which 131 hotels and 11,811 rooms are operational. Keys RevPAR grew 20% and Aurika 19% for FY25 to FY26 on management's figures.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (owned/leased)
segments.commentary: Post-scheme, Fleur to have 5,600 rooms across 39 operational hotels; 4 hotels with 875 rooms in confirmed pipeline, including 572 rooms at Nehru Place (estimated capex Rs 700 crore). Fees Rs 95.8 crore, +8% on a same-store basis.

segments.name: Aurika brand
segments.commentary: Highest ARR and margin product; Aurika occupancy rose from 62% to 74% for FY26 with RevPAR +19%, though Q4 occupancy fell 2% as a large Mumbai wet-lease ended. Aurika has only two hotels (Mumbai and Udaipur).

guidance_outlook: Cost heads (GST impact, technology, renovation) expected to fall from 5.8% of revenue in FY26 to about 4.8% in FY27 and 3.7% in FY28 onward, adding roughly 1% of revenue a year, plus Rs 25-30 crore of one-off costs (Delhi property tax ex gratia, labour code) that drop out from FY27.
FY27 renovation spend about 1.9% of revenue, normal renovation thereafter at about 1.3% (possibly 1.0-1.2%); GST impact rising from 1% to 2% of revenue in FY27 as it becomes a full year.
Expected openings of about 2,000 rooms in FY27, rising to about 3,000 in FY28 and 4,000 in FY29; management says openings lag signings by about three years, with signings of about 5,000 rooms a year.

Lemon Tree standalone post-demerger: steady-state flow-through on management fees of 75-80%, currently about 60% pro forma; steady-state PAT about 60% of revenue (per management, after tax and no interest or depreciation).

Fleur targets up to Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital over 12-18 months (including Warburg primary investment), and plans to add about 2,500 rooms; management does not give fee guidance for FY27-28.
Demerger: CCI approval received in April; SEBI and shareholder/creditor approvals underway; NCLT timing 6-18 months, with management giving 12-18 months as the outer limit.
Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt may rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed, temporarily.
capex_capacity: Renovation: about 5,000 rooms to be renovated, of which 4,000 heavy renovation with about 85% complete; about 400-500 rooms under renovation in Q4 and similar in Q1.
Keys Whitefield renovation expected to complete in about 4 months; Keys Hosur Road under renovation; Keys Pimpri, Pune completed.
Aurika Naldehra, Shimla: 2 of 3 blocks to open by Q2 FY27 for the summer season.
Aurika Varanasi: 47-room heritage licence signed January 2026 on the ghat by the Ganges.

Nehru Place (572 rooms, North India's largest hotel) awaiting final approval before construction; estimated Rs 700 crore; Andaz (525 rooms) nearby, with cash flow over 3.5 years, 60% in the last 18 months.
Acquisition valuations cited at 8x-16x EBITDA; greenfield build 3-4 years, renovation-led acquisitions 1-2 years, operating assets immediate.
demand_pricing: Mid-March decision to prioritise occupancy over rate; April-May tactical pricing to keep an occupancy premium, with ARR roughly flat YoY; Q4 occupancy reached what management called a ceiling.

Corporate travel slowed in March as companies cut travel due to fares and the war; corporate share of occupancy fell to 55% from 59% in Q4 (negotiated room nights 55.4% for the full year vs 56.1%). Retail filled the gap at lower rates.
Indigo shutdown in December and the Middle East war (from early March, continuing into April) cited as headwinds; May described as surprisingly good.
Mumbai micro-market saw about 2,000 keys added in the last year (from Accor Fairmont to Ginger), creating a temporary supply glut for Aurika Mumbai.
Target: 65% of business from retail (direct, B2C, loyalty) once the portfolio reaches 20,000-25,000 operating rooms.
Loyalty programme has about 24 lakh members, driving about 25% of room nights per management.
Indian mid-market: management says demand outpaces supply; cites 2.5 million unbranded rooms in India as a conversion opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Would Fleur's inventory be managed by a non-Lemon Tree operator post-demerger, and how would that work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fleur is brand-agnostic and would choose whichever brand makes economic sense, while Lemon Tree should not be discriminated against; it cited a lost 5-star NCLT bid as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Why Aurika RevPAR growth (3%) lags Keys (16%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to micro-market differences and timing; full-year FY26 RevPAR growth was 19% for Aurika and 20% for Keys, with Keys set to keep growing as renovations finish.

qa_highlights.question: How confident are you on conversion of signings into openings, and what fee numbers for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings lag signings by about three years; management declined to give fee guidance but expects about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-saving path and steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Renovation, GST and technology costs to fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28; pro forma Lemon Tree flow-through is about 60% now, targeted at 70%+ and then 75-80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: CCI approval came in April; SEBI/shareholder/creditor steps underway; NCLT is the main variable, with 12-18 months the outer limit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did incentive-linked management fees lag for third-party hotels versus Fleur?
qa_highlights.answer: Incentive fees (1-5% of revenue depending on GOP slab) fell as renovation and GST cut owned-hotel EBITDA margins; third-party fees rose 23% from net additions, Fleur fees rose 8% on a same-store basis.

qa_highlights.question: What peak debt level is comfortable after Fleur's deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt could rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore temporarily if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation for standalone Lemon Tree post-demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Lemon Tree to be debt-free and cash-generative; Board to decide a dividend or buyback policy; no F&B expansion planned, with a high hurdle for acquisitions.

risks_watch: NCLT timing for the Fleur demerger: management guides 6-18 months, with 12-18 months as the outer limit; CCI approval received in April, SEBI, shareholder and creditor steps still pending.

Demand softness: corporate share of occupancy fell to 55% in Q4 from 59%; March and April were weak on the Middle East conflict and airline disruption, though management said May was surprisingly good.

Margin recovery depends on renovation spend falling to about 1.9% of revenue in FY27 and GST impact and technology costs easing; standalone flow-through is about 60% pro forma versus a 70%+ steady-state target.
Openings execution: about 2,000 rooms targeted in FY27 versus 1,523 rooms opened in FY26; openings lag signings by about three years and owner-finance delays could cause slippage.

Leverage post-deployment: consolidated debt could rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore from about Rs 1,500 crore if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed, versus debt-to-EBITDA of about 2.25x now; Fleur's 2,500-room pipeline is not yet firm.
Aurika weakness: Q4 occupancy fell 2% after a large Mumbai wet-lease ended and Mumbai micro-market supply rose by about 2,000 keys; Keys RevPAR growth depends on completing renovations.
key_quotes: FY26 was the best year in Lemon Tree's history across Occupancy, ARR, Revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT, Cash Profit and Q4 FY26 was the best ever fourth quarter on the same parameters.
I want to take this opportunity to continue the conversation on the demerger scheme.
I do not want to give guidance, but I can give you a direction.
Corporate travel is the first that kind of dries up when war happens because it is under the control normally of the CEO or an equivalent CXO and it is a one -person decision.
Lemon Tree will not need any significant capital other than potentially investments in technology or in marketing and so on.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year record, the long-term margin path and the demerger, but cautious and evasive on near-term demand, the war's duration, and specific guidance; management repeatedly declined to give fee or revenue numbers for FY27-28 and to predict the NCLT timeline. Tone on the Q4 softness was defensive, attributing weakness to Indigo, the war and Mumbai supply.
